title: When a High Count Is Not Yet a Diagnosis: CMML, Eosinophilic MLN-TK, HLH and Mononucleosis
summary: Learn the sustained-count and exclusion rules for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, why PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions respond to imatinib while FGFR1 fusions do not, how the HLH-2004 five-of-eight framework beats a single ferritin, and the limits of heterophile testing in infectious mononucleosis.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 34 High-Yield Hits 7 (CMML criteria), 14 (PDGFRA imatinib-sensitive, FGFR1 not), 15 (HLH) and 16 (infectious mononucleosis triad, heterophile, CMV mimic). Checked against Loghavi 2026, Valent 2019, Metzgeroth 2023, Kim 2021, Balfour 2015 and Ishii 2019. Three divergences are flagged: the monocyte threshold in Hit 7 is the WHO 2016 figure, lowered to ≥0.5 ×10⁹/L by the WHO 5th edition and the ICC (register flag rv-cmml-amc-threshold); the "~60% die within 2 months without etoposide" figure in Hit 15 is not supported by the sources read (rv-hlh-two-month-mortality); and "positive heterophile = EBV" in Hit 16 needs the heterophile caveats (rv-im-heterophile-limits). FGFR1 is now targetable with pemigatinib (rv-fgfr1-pemigatinib). Not taught: the Number Vault table, CMML-0/1/2 blast tiers, CMML prognostic scores, HLH treatment protocols, mononucleosis complications.

objectives: State the sustained absolute and relative monocyte criteria for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia and the exclusions it requires.
Explain why PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions are imatinib-responsive while FGFR1 fusions are not.
Apply the HLH-2004 five-of-eight framework instead of relying on a single ferritin value.
Interpret heterophile and Epstein-Barr-virus-specific antibody results in suspected infectious mononucleosis.

scenes.title: Four high counts, one morning
scenes.altText: Invented scenario. Four results land together: (1) a 71-year-old with monocytes 2.4 ×10⁹/L, 18% of leukocytes, the third such count in four months, marrow blasts 4%; (2) a 42-year-old man with eosinophils 8.6 ×10⁹/L and monocytes 1.3 ×10⁹/L; (3) an adult with fever, pancytopenia and ferritin 14,000 µg/L; (4) a 19-year-old with fever, exudative pharyngitis, posterior cervical nodes and Downey atypical lymphocytes. Question token: “Which of these counts is already the diagnosis?”

cues.text: Four high counts arrive on the same morning. A seventy-one-year-old has monocytes of two point four, eighteen percent of leukocytes, for the third time in four months.
A forty-two-year-old man has eosinophils of eight point six and monocytes of one point three. An adult has fever, pancytopenia and a ferritin of fourteen thousand.
A nineteen-year-old has fever, exudative pharyngitis, posterior cervical nodes and Downey cells on the smear. Which of these counts is already the diagnosis?

scenes.title: What each count means before any label
scenes.altText: Four definition cards. Monocytosis for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia (CMML) is counted twice over: an absolute monocyte count AND monocytes ≥10% of blood leukocytes, sustained — optimally at least 3 months. Eosinophilia: hypereosinophilia is >1.5 ×10⁹/L, but in the registry cohort of myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) hypereosinophilia was present in 91% of FIP1L1::PDGFRA cases yet only 43% of PDGFRB, FGFR1 and JAK2 cases, and monocytosis >1 ×10⁹/L occurred in 27–33% — so these neoplasms can look like CMML. Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is not a count at all: HLH-2004 asks for a molecular diagnosis or 5 of 8 criteria. Infectious mononucleosis is a clinical entity — pharyngitis, cervical node enlargement, fatigue and fever — and its Downey atypical lymphocytes are activated CD8-positive T cells responding to Epstein-Barr-virus-infected B cells.

cues.text: Start with the definitions. Monocytosis for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia is counted twice over: an absolute monocyte count, and monocytes at least ten percent of blood leukocytes, sustained, optimally for at least three months.

Hypereosinophilia means eosinophils above one point five. But in a registry of myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine kinase fusions, hypereosinophilia was present in ninety-one percent of FIP1L1-PDGFRA cases and only forty-three percent of the others, and a quarter to a third also had monocytosis. So these neoplasms can imitate chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia.
Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is not a count. The HLH two thousand four rules ask for a molecular diagnosis, or five of eight criteria.

Infectious mononucleosis is a clinical entity: pharyngitis, cervical node enlargement, fatigue and fever. Its Downey atypical lymphocytes are activated CD8 T cells responding to virus-infected B cells.

scenes.title: The threshold moved, and the genotype decides
scenes.altText: Three change cards. (1) CMML threshold: the WHO 5th edition and the International Consensus Classification both lowered the absolute monocyte count from 1.0 to ≥0.5 ×10⁹/L while keeping monocytes ≥10% of leukocytes; cases in the 0.5 to under 1.0 range (oligomonocytic CMML) require cytogenetic or molecular evidence of clonality, and the WHO 5th edition mandates both clonality and dysplasia there. CMML also needs <20% blasts and absence of BCR::ABL1 AND of the other tyrosine kinase fusions that define MLN-TK. (2) Genotype decides the drug: imatinib is highly effective for PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions — overall survival 92% at 5 and 10 years for FIP1L1::PDGFRA and 78% at 5 and 10 years for PDGFRB — whereas FGFR1 fusions are not imatinib-responsive, with 57% survival at 5 years; ponatinib had limited efficacy and pemigatinib showed promising phase-2 results. (3) Epstein-Barr serology: viral capsid antigen IgM is present in only about 75% of acute cases and can be falsely positive in cytomegalovirus infection, capsid IgG develops in all patients, and nuclear antigen 1 IgG is usually undetectable for 90 days or more, so finding it during an acute illness rules out acute primary Epstein-Barr infection.

cues.text: Two thresholds moved. The WHO fifth edition and the International Consensus Classification both lowered the absolute monocyte count for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia from one point zero to at least nought point five, keeping the ten percent rule. In that lower band, called oligomonocytic, proof of clonality is required.
The disease still needs under twenty percent blasts, and absence not only of BCR-ABL1 but of the other tyrosine kinase fusions that define the eosinophilic neoplasms.

In those neoplasms the genotype decides the drug. Imatinib works on PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions: survival was ninety-two percent at five and ten years for FIP1L1-PDGFRA. FGFR1 fusions do not respond, with fifty-seven percent at five years, though pemigatinib looks promising.

For Epstein-Barr virus, capsid IgM appears in only about three quarters of acute cases and can be falsely positive in cytomegalovirus infection. Nuclear antigen one IgG takes ninety days or more, so finding it during the acute illness rules out a primary infection.

props.label: < 20% blasts · exclude BCR::ABL1 and TK fusions

scenes.title: Read the four results
scenes.altText: Four answer cards for the hook. (1) Monocytes 2.4 ×10⁹/L, 18% of leukocytes, sustained beyond three months, blasts 4%: the monocyte criteria are met under both the old and the new threshold, but the diagnosis still needs dysplasia, abnormal monocyte partitioning or a clonal abnormality, and exclusion of BCR::ABL1 and other tyrosine kinase fusions. (2) Eosinophils 8.6 ×10⁹/L with monocytosis: test for PDGFRA, PDGFRB and FGFR1 fusions first, because monocytosis occurs in 27–33% of these neoplasms and the fusion changes both the diagnosis and the drug. (3) Ferritin 14,000 µg/L: the HLH-2004 ferritin criterion is only ≥500 µg/L and marked hyperferritinaemia is non-specific in adults — of 113 adults with ferritin above 50,000 µg/L only 19 had HLH — so count the criteria (fever ≥38.5 °C for ≥7 days, splenomegaly, cytopenias in ≥2 of 3 lineages, fasting triglycerides ≥265 mg/dL and/or fibrinogen ≤1.5 g/L, haemophagocytosis, low or absent natural killer activity, ferritin ≥500 µg/L, soluble CD25 ≥2400 U/mL) and look for a trigger. (4) Triad plus Downey cells plus a positive heterophile fits Epstein-Barr virus, but heterophile antibodies can persist a year or more, roughly 40% of children 4 years or younger never make them, and cytomegalovirus causes 5–16% of mononucleosis in older patients with milder nodes and pharyngitis but more hepatitis.

cues.text: Result one meets the monocyte rules under both the old and the new threshold, but you still need dysplasia, abnormal monocyte partitioning or a clonal abnormality, and you must exclude BCR-ABL1 and the other tyrosine kinase fusions.
Result two: order fusion testing first. A quarter to a third of these eosinophilic neoplasms also have monocytosis, and the fusion changes both the label and the drug.

Result three: the ferritin criterion is only five hundred, and marked hyperferritinaemia is non-specific in adults. Of a hundred and thirteen adults with ferritin above fifty thousand, only nineteen had the disease. Count the criteria and hunt the trigger.

Result four fits Epstein-Barr virus, but heterophile antibodies can persist a year or more, about forty percent of children four or younger never make them, and cytomegalovirus causes five to sixteen percent of cases.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards. “One monocyte count above the cut-off is chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia” (✓ the count must be sustained, be ≥10% of leukocytes, carry clonality or dysplasia, and tyrosine kinase fusions must be excluded). “An eosinophilic myeloid neoplasm means imatinib” (✓ only PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions; FGFR1 fusions are not imatinib-responsive and survival was 57% at 5 years). “Ferritin in the thousands means haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis” (✓ the criterion is ≥500 µg/L and marked hyperferritinaemia is non-specific in adults; you need 5 of 8 criteria or a molecular diagnosis).

cues.text: Trap one: one monocyte count above the cut-off is chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia. No. It must be sustained, relative as well as absolute, clonal, and other fusions must be excluded.
Trap two: an eosinophilic myeloid neoplasm means imatinib. No. Only PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions respond; FGFR1 fusions do not.
Trap three: ferritin in the thousands means haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. No. The criterion is five hundred, and high ferritin is non-specific in adults.

props.title: ✗ “Eosinophilic neoplasm = imatinib.”
lines: ✓ PDGFRA/PDGFRB yes · FGFR1 no (57% at 5 y)

scenes.title: Clock, clone, clear
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “A count is a headline, not a diagnosis. For the chronic myeloid entities you need the CLOCK (monocytosis sustained about three months), the CLONE (dysplasia, abnormal monocyte partitioning or a molecular lesion) and the CLEAR list (BCR::ABL1 and the other tyrosine kinase fusions ruled out).” Tokens: clock, clone, clear. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: a count is a headline, not a diagnosis. For the chronic myeloid entities you need the clock, monocytosis sustained about three months; the clone, dysplasia or abnormal monocyte partitioning or a molecular lesion; and the clear list, BCR-ABL1 and the other tyrosine kinase fusions ruled out.

Where it breaks: haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and mononucleosis have no clone and no three-month clock, one is a five-of-eight syndrome counted in days and the other an acute infection; and the monocyte threshold itself differs between the older and the newer classifications.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Count → clock + clone + exclusions”, “PDGFRA/PDGFRB imatinib · FGFR1 not · HLH 5 of 8 · heterophile is imperfect”.

cues.text: A single high count is never the diagnosis, because chronic monocytosis needs persistence, a clonal or phenotypic marker and exclusion of tyrosine kinase fusions, eosinophilic neoplasms are sorted by genotype since only rearranged PDGFRA and PDGFRB respond to imatinib, haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis needs five of eight criteria rather than a high ferritin, and the mononucleosis triad still needs serology the heterophile test cannot always give.

props.label: PDGFRA/PDGFRB → imatinib · FGFR1 → no · HLH 5 of 8 · heterophile imperfect

explanation.what: Plain language: four white-cell problems where a single high number tempts you into a diagnosis you have not earned. Chronic monocytosis may be a clonal marrow disease or a reaction; a high eosinophil count may hide a fusion gene that decides the drug; a sky-high ferritin may or may not be a cytokine storm; and a classic sore-throat illness still needs the right antibody test. Scientific terms: chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia (CMML), absolute monocyte count (AMC), oligomonocytic CMML, monocyte subset partitioning (classical Mo1 monocytes, CD14++CD16−), myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK), FIP1L1::PDGFRA, PDGFRB and FGFR1 rearrangements, imatinib, pemigatinib, haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), HLH-2004 criteria, soluble CD25, heterophile antibody, viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM and IgG, Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA-1) IgG, Downey atypical lymphocytes.
explanation.why: Each of these diagnoses carries a different action. CMML commits a patient to a myeloid neoplasm pathway, so it must be sustained, clonal and free of the tyrosine kinase fusions that would instead be treated with a kinase inhibitor. In MLN-TK the fusion gene, not the eosinophil count, predicts survival. In HLH the whole point of the criteria is that no one finding, including ferritin, is specific enough in adults. In mononucleosis a negative heterophile in a young child, or a positive one left over from last year, misleads unless specific serology is used.
explanation.measure: CMML: sustained monocytosis — WHO 2016 and the Valent 2019 consensus require AMC ≥1.0 ×10⁹/L, the WHO 5th edition and the ICC require ≥0.5 ×10⁹/L — with monocytes ≥10% of blood leukocytes, optimally for at least 3 months, <20% blasts, absence of BCR::ABL1 and other tyrosine kinase fusions, plus dysplasia, abnormal monocyte partitioning (classical Mo1 monocytes >94% of blood monocytes) or a clonal abnormality; in the 0.5 to <1.0 ×10⁹/L band clonality is mandatory. MLN-TK: hypereosinophilia >1.5 ×10⁹/L; FIP1L1::PDGFRA overall survival 92% at 5 and 10 years on imatinib, PDGFRB 78% at 5 and 10 years, FGFR1 57% at 5 years. HLH-2004: a molecular diagnosis, or 5 of 8 — fever ≥38.5 °C for ≥7 days, splenomegaly, cytopenias in ≥2 of 3 lineages (haemoglobin <9 g/dL, platelets <100 ×10⁹/L, neutrophils <1.0 ×10⁹/L), fasting triglycerides ≥265 mg/dL and/or fibrinogen ≤1.5 g/L, haemophagocytosis, low or absent natural killer activity, ferritin ≥500 µg/L, soluble CD25 ≥2400 U/mL. Mononucleosis: VCA IgM in about 75% of acute cases, VCA IgG in all, EBNA-1 IgG usually undetectable for ≥90 days.
explanation.differs: CMML vs MLN-TK with monocytosis (fusion testing separates them); PDGFRA/PDGFRB vs FGFR1 fusions (imatinib response and survival); ferritin as one criterion vs ferritin as the diagnosis; Epstein-Barr vs cytomegalovirus mononucleosis (age, severity of nodes and pharyngitis, hepatitis, heterophile and specific serology).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: decide whether a monocytosis vignette has met the CMML rules and what must still be excluded; pick the patient whose eosinophilic neoplasm will respond to imatinib; recognise that a high ferritin alone does not establish HLH; choose the next test after a negative heterophile in a young child.

mnemonic.text: A count is a headline, not a diagnosis. For the chronic myeloid entities you need the CLOCK (monocytosis sustained about three months), the CLONE (dysplasia, abnormal monocyte partitioning or a molecular lesion) and the CLEAR list (BCR::ABL1 and the other tyrosine kinase fusions ruled out).
mnemonic.explanation: Separates a single abnormal number from the duration, clonality and exclusion evidence a neoplastic label needs.
mnemonic.limitation: It fits only the chronic myeloid entities: haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis has no clone and no three-month clock (it is a five-of-eight syndrome assessed over days), infectious mononucleosis is an acute infection, and the monocyte threshold itself differs between the WHO 2016 and the WHO 5th edition/ICC rules.

Survival percentages come from one European registry cohort and are not general population estimates.
takeaway: A single high count is never the diagnosis, because chronic monocytosis needs persistence, a clonal or phenotypic marker and exclusion of tyrosine kinase fusions, eosinophilic neoplasms are sorted by genotype since only rearranged PDGFRA and PDGFRB respond to imatinib, haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis needs five of eight criteria rather than a high ferritin, and the mononucleosis triad still needs serology the heterophile test cannot always give.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old has had monocytes of 1.8 ×10⁹/L making up 15% of leukocytes on three counts over four months, with 5% marrow blasts and dysplastic megakaryocytes. Which result would most clearly exclude chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia?

options.text: A FIP1L1::PDGFRA fusion on molecular testing
options.rationale: Correct. A tyrosine kinase fusion defines a myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with tyrosine kinase gene fusions, and chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia requires the absence of BCR::ABL1 and of these other fusions.

options.text: Classical Mo1 monocytes making up 96% of blood monocytes
options.rationale: Incorrect. Abnormal monocyte subset partitioning with Mo1 above 94% supports the diagnosis rather than excluding it.

options.text: A TET2 mutation with a variant allele fraction of 40%
options.rationale: Incorrect. TET2 is one of the commonest drivers in this disease and supplies the clonal evidence the diagnosis needs.
Incorrect. Splenomegaly is a common feature of the disease and is not an exclusion.

questions.stem: Two patients have a myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia: one carries FIP1L1::PDGFRA and the other an FGFR1 fusion. Which statement matches the registry data?

options.text: The PDGFRA patient should respond durably to imatinib, while the FGFR1 patient should not
options.rationale: Correct. Imatinib is highly effective in PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions, with 92% survival at 5 and 10 years for FIP1L1::PDGFRA, whereas FGFR1 fusions are not imatinib-responsive and showed 57% survival at 5 years.

options.text: Both should respond to imatinib because both are tyrosine kinase fusions
options.rationale: Incorrect. Being a kinase fusion is not enough; imatinib does not inhibit FGFR1.

options.text: The FGFR1 patient has the better prognosis because eosinophilia is milder
options.rationale: Incorrect. Hypereosinophilia was actually less frequent outside the PDGFRA group, and FGFR1 carried the worse survival.

options.text: Neither genotype matters once the eosinophil count exceeds 1.5 ×10⁹/L
options.rationale: Incorrect. The fusion, not the eosinophil count, drives treatment choice and outcome.

questions.stem: An adult inpatient has a ferritin of 38,000 µg/L, fever for three days and mild thrombocytopenia. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Marked hyperferritinaemia alone does not establish haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis; assess the full criteria set
options.rationale: Correct. The HLH-2004 ferritin criterion is only ≥500 µg/L, and marked hyperferritinaemia is non-specific in adults, so a molecular diagnosis or 5 of 8 criteria is required.

options.text: A ferritin above 10,000 µg/L is diagnostic in adults
options.rationale: Incorrect. That figure comes from a paediatric study; in adults ferritin is often raised for other reasons.

options.text: A normal fibrinogen rules the diagnosis out
options.rationale: Incorrect. Hypertriglyceridaemia and hypofibrinogenaemia form a single criterion, and a patient can still reach five of eight without it.

options.text: Absence of haemophagocytosis on marrow examination rules the diagnosis out
options.rationale: Incorrect. Haemophagocytosis is one of eight criteria, not a mandatory finding.

claims.text: CMML needs sustained absolute and relative (≥10%) monocytosis, optimally ≥3 months, with <20% blasts, exclusion of BCR::ABL1 and other tyrosine kinase fusions, plus dysplasia, abnormal Mo1 partitioning or a clonal abnormality.

The absolute monocyte count threshold is ≥1.0 ×10⁹/L in WHO 2016 and the Valent 2019 consensus but ≥0.5 ×10⁹/L in the WHO 5th edition and the ICC, where clonality is mandatory in the 0.5 to <1.0 band.

Imatinib is highly effective in PDGFRA and PDGFRB fusions (FIP1L1::PDGFRA 92% survival at 5 and 10 years; PDGFRB 78%) but FGFR1 fusions are not imatinib-responsive (57% at 5 years), with pemigatinib promising in phase 2.
Hypereosinophilia is not obligatory outside PDGFRA (91% vs 43%) and monocytosis >1 ×10⁹/L occurs in 27–33% of MLN-TK, so these neoplasms overlap with the CMML presentation.
HLH-2004 requires a molecular diagnosis or 5 of 8 criteria, with ferritin ≥500 µg/L as only one of them.
Marked hyperferritinaemia is non-specific in adults: of 113 adults with ferritin above 50,000 µg/L only 19 had HLH.
The mononucleosis picture is pharyngitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, fatigue and fever, and Downey atypical lymphocytes are activated CD8-positive T cells responding to infected B cells.

Heterophile testing is imperfect (about 40% of children ≤4 years do not develop it, it can persist a year or more, false positives occur); VCA IgM is positive in about 75% of acute cases with false positives especially in cytomegalovirus infection, and EBNA-1 IgG during acute illness rules out acute primary infection.
Cytomegalovirus causes 5–16% of mononucleosis, in patients 10–15 years older with milder nodes and pharyngitis but more hepatitis and thrombocytopenia.
The reviewer figure that about 60% die within 2 months of HLH without etoposide-based therapy.
claims.note: Not supported by the sources read; not taught. Kim 2021 reports 4-year survival of 90.4% with early etoposide versus 56.5% without in paediatric Epstein-Barr-virus-associated HLH. See register flag rv-hlh-two-month-mortality.

claims.text: Four-result scenario invented; criteria shown as schematic cards.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 34 Hit 7 gives the CMML monocyte threshold as >1 ×10⁹/L. Loghavi 2026 states that the WHO 5th edition and the ICC both lowered the defining absolute monocyte count from 1.0 to ≥0.5 ×10⁹/L, with clonality required (and dysplasia under the WHO 5th edition) in the 0.5 to <1.0 band. Hit 7 also lists only BCR-ABL1 as an exclusion, whereas the other tyrosine kinase fusions must also be excluded (register flag rv-cmml-amc-threshold).

Ch. 34 Hit 15 states that about 60% of HLH patients die within 2 months without etoposide-based therapy. No source read in this session supports that figure; Kim 2021 reports 4-year survival of 90.4% with etoposide within 4 weeks versus 56.5% without in paediatric Epstein-Barr-virus-associated HLH. The lesson teaches the criteria and the ferritin caveat instead (register flag rv-hlh-two-month-mortality).

Ch. 34 Hit 16 equates a positive heterophile test with Epstein-Barr virus and a negative one with cytomegalovirus. Balfour 2015 notes that about 40% of children 4 years or younger never develop heterophile antibodies, that heterophile antibodies can persist a year or more so are not always diagnostic of acute infection, and that VCA IgM can be falsely positive in cytomegalovirus infection (register flag rv-im-heterophile-limits).

Ch. 34 Hit 14 says FGFR1-rearranged disease "is not" imatinib-sensitive and has a poor prognosis, without noting that it is now targetable: Metzgeroth 2023 reports promising phase-2 results for pemigatinib in FGFR1 fusions (register flag rv-fgfr1-pemigatinib).
